findings.title: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard method is never called
findings.body: The _create_process_for_shard method (lines 127-132) is defined but never called. The _ensure_processes_alive method calls _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards) directly, not _create_process_for_shard. This is dead code that should be removed or the call site should be updated to use it.

findings.title: Inconsistent default for flusher_processes between CLI and factory
findings.body: The CLI option --flusher-processes defaults to 1, but the factory parameter flusher_processes defaults to None, which becomes len(buffer.assigned_shards) in the flusher (via `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`). This means direct callers of the factory (e.g., tests) get a different default (one process per shard) than CLI users (1 process). This is a behavior change from the old code, which always created exactly 1 process regardless of shard count. Direct callers that don't pass flusher_processes and have multiple partitions will get N processes instead of 1.

findings.title: test_flusher_processes_limit does not verify actual flushing with multiple processes
findings.body: The test_flusher_processes_limit test only verifies the process count (len(flusher.processes) == 2) and shard distribution (total_shards == 4), but does not verify that the flusher actually works correctly with multiple processes. Since the main purpose of this PR is to introduce multiprocessed flushing, the test should submit messages to all shards, trigger flushing, and verify that all messages are correctly flushed across the multiple processes. Without this, a bug in the multi-process flushing logic could go undetected.

findings.title: CLI help text is misleading about the default behavior
findings.body: The help text says 'Maximum number of processes for the span flusher. Defaults to 1.' but this is only true for CLI usage. The factory parameter flusher_processes defaults to None, which results in one process per shard when called directly. The help text should clarify that the default is 1 for the CLI, and that the factory default is None (meaning one process per shard).

findings.title: Naming inconsistency: flusher_processes vs max_processes
findings.body: The parameter is called flusher_processes in the CLI option and factory, but max_processes in the SpanFlusher constructor. This naming inconsistency could be confusing for maintainers. Consider using the same name across all layers (e.g., flusher_processes everywhere).
